On the basis of orientation of animals

1. Klinotaxis: It is the turning movement of animal by successive comparison of stimulus intensities. Some animals lack distinct sense organs but they possess receptor cells at the antero-dorsal side of the body. Such organisms respond by comparing stimulus intensities of both sides by bending their head first in one direction and in another direction. This process continues until both sides are equally stimulated. Example: Maggots of housefly, Euglena etc. move in this way or show wavy movement with light stimulus of different intensities thrown from two sides.

2. Tropotaxis: It is the straight orientation of organism in which organism moves either towards or away from stimulus. No lateral or wavy movement of organism as in klinotaxis is found. It is found in bilaterally symmetrical animals having paired sense organ where these organs compare stimulus intensities of both side simultaneously and show straight movement. Example: Tick and lice show positive phototropotaxis.

3. Telotaxis: If two sources of stimuli of equal intensity operated at the same time, animal orients to any one stimulus but not both or intermediate. Example: In morning time, honey bee moves with light but rest on flower when it finds. But while returning hive, uses source of light. In above case, flower and sunlight are two stimuli operating at the same time.

4. Menotaxis: It is the orientation or movement of organism towards a stimulus at certain angle. It is also called ‘light compass response’. Example: Insects like honey bee, ants, beetle (Geotrapes sylvaticus) etc make constant angle to the sunlight while returning home. If direction of sunlight is changed apparently using mirror, they also change their path.

5. Mnemotaxis: Movement of organism in response to complex stimuli situations is called Mnemotaxis. Example: Hunting wasp uses a number of stimuli such as landmarks, light direction, trails of chemical left by them etc. while returning their nest. Similarly, many long distant migratory birds while returning their original home ground use a number of stimuli like land mark, coastal line, river, mountain range, celestial bodies etc.
9.2.4 DOMINANCE

It is a type of social behaviour in which an individual dominates other members of the society or group by aggression or threat or by any other means. In the social animals, it is necessary to keep all the members of the society under control. The dominating animal has higher chances of getting food, mate, shelter and other resources. Dominance is determined by various factors like age, sex, experience, morphology and physiological status of an animal. In most cases, older one dominates young one, stronger is dominating over weak one, bigger to smaller one, male to female. There are several ways by which dominant animal sub-ordinates or suppresses other member and some examples are given below:

1. Newly matured song bird dominates older bird by singing beautifully while attracting female for mating.
2. Dog defends its territory by snoring and posing teeth when it encounters other dogs. The dominated dog runs away by lowering tail.
3. Dominant animal occupies middle position in the herd of cattle while finding resources. 4. Many male dogs gather around and move in with dominant female dog during breeding

season. This phenomenon is also found in Lemur. 5. When two unfamiliar buffalos encounter suddenly in grassland, each of them start showing their aggressiveness by pawing ground, head -butting, shoving or even charging. Also found among goats, oxen etc.

9.2.5 LEADERSHIP

It is also an innate behaviour of animal in which an individual lead and guide other members in a group. A leader occupies the highest rank or hierarchy level irrespective of age and sex. Leadership is an ability of individual animal to lead and provide proper guidance. This type of social behaviour is needed at the time of moving in group, finding resources, migration, defending territories, fighting with enemies and many more. A real leader mostly initiates, stabilizes and integrates the activities o a group members. Leadership can be seen in some animals like ant, deer, sheep, kangaroo etc. A leader gets better priority of food, place, mate etc.
